title.es: Ser el invitado de un pódcast

es: Participar como invitado en un pódcast: responder con historias, devolver una pregunta de sondeo y cerrar con una síntesis.

teaching.en: Thanks for having me; I am delighted to be your guest today.
teaching.es: Gracias por invitarme; estoy encantado de ser tu invitado hoy.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura cálida: Thanks for having me (for + -ing) y guest para tu papel.
segments: Thanks for having me; I am
delighted to be your guest today.
teaching.audioText: Thanks for having me; I am delighted to be your guest today.

teaching.en: Let me answer that briefly, with a story from my first year of volunteering.
teaching.es: Déjame responder eso brevemente, con una historia de mi primer año de voluntariado.
teaching.explanationEs: Anuncia una respuesta estructurada: briefly te da tiempo y marca que habrá una historia.
segments: Let me answer that briefly, with a
story from my first year of volunteering.
teaching.audioText: Let me answer that briefly, with a story from my first year of volunteering.

teaching.en: If I may turn that around, what drew you to this episode?
teaching.es: Si me permites devolverte la pregunta, ¿qué te atrajo de este episodio?
teaching.explanationEs: If I may turn that around devuelve una pregunta de sondeo al anfitrión con cortesía.
segments: If I may turn that around,
what drew you to this episode?
teaching.audioText: If I may turn that around, what drew you to this episode?

teaching.en: To what extent do your listeners expect guests to disagree?
teaching.es: ¿Hasta qué punto esperan tus oyentes que los invitados discrepen?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta de sondeo directa: To what extent + do + sujeto.
teaching.audioText: To what extent do your listeners expect guests to disagree?

teaching.en: If there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start before you feel ready.
teaching.es: Si hay una idea que los oyentes deben llevarse, es esta: empezar antes de sentirte preparado.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre con síntesis: one takeaway + idea clave, y wrap up para concluir.
segments: If there is one takeaway for the listeners,
it is this: start before you feel ready.
teaching.audioText: If there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start before you feel ready.

teaching.en: Honestly, the hardest part was asking for help.
teaching.es: Sinceramente, lo más difícil fue pedir ayuda.
teaching.explanationEs: Honestly introduce una respuesta franca antes del ejemplo o la historia.
teaching.audioText: Honestly, the hardest part was asking for help.

prompt.es: Une cada frase de pódcast con su función.

pairs: If I may turn that around, …
If there is one takeaway, it is this: …

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple un paso del pódcast: abrir, devolver la pregunta, cerrar con una idea clave y anunciar una respuesta estructurada.

hint.es: Piensa en el orden de un pódcast: empezar, responder, preguntar y terminar.

pairs: If I may turn that around, …
If there is one takeaway, it is this: …

feedback.es: Tras la preposición for, el verbo toma -ing: Thanks for having me.

hint.es: Después de una preposición el verbo va en -ing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Si me permites, te devuelvo la pregunta.»

answer.text: If I may turn that question around

feedback.es: If I may turn that around es la forma cortés de devolver una pregunta al anfitrión.

hint.es: Tras may, el verbo va en forma base y sin to.

prompt.es: Escucha a la presentadora y elige qué pide.

choices.text: She asks the guest to describe his family.
She asks how long the episode is.
She asks for the key message of the conversation.

feedback.es: «One takeaway» es la idea principal que deben recordar los oyentes: pide una síntesis final.

origin.audio: Before we finish, what is the one takeaway you would like our listeners to remember?

prompt.es: ¿Qué pregunta de sondeo puede devolver el invitado?

choices.text: To what extent do you think listeners want advice?
To what extent you think listeners want advice?
To what extent think you listeners want advice?

feedback.es: To what extent abre una pregunta directa y lleva auxiliar: do you think.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le falta a esta respuesta del invitado?

choices.text: A concrete example and a result.

feedback.es: Responde con «things went wrong sometimes»: no hay ejemplo concreto ni resultado medible.

origin.text:
Host: Tell me about a time when things went wrong.
Guest: Things went wrong sometimes, and it was fine.

prompt.es: Escribe las respuestas del invitado: apertura, historia, reto, pregunta y cierre.

answer.text: Thanks for having me. I am delighted to be your guest today. You asked what led me to start the volunteer club. Briefly, it began last year, when I was in charge of a small recycling project at school. When I arrived, nobody had emptied the bins for weeks, so I drew up a rota and asked each class to choose a captain. As a result, our recycling rate has doubled since then. You also asked about my biggest challenge. Honestly, it was keeping everyone interested. For example, in November only six students came, but after I created a short checklist, attendance rose from six to twenty. If I may turn that around, to what extent do your listeners already take part in projects like this? To wrap up, if there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start small, and ask for help early. The experience taught me that clear responsibility prevents most problems. Thank you again for the invitation.

To wrap up, if there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start small, and ask for help early. The experience taught me that clear responsibility prevents most problems. Thank you for inviting me. It is a pleasure to be a guest on the show. You asked why I joined the project. Briefly, last spring I was in charge of the school garden, and nobody had watered the plants for a month. I made a watering rota, and as a result, the garden has given vegetables every summer since then. Your second question was about my biggest challenge. Honestly, it was finding volunteers. For example, in March only three students helped, but after I created a simple poster and a checklist, the team grew from three to fifteen. If I may turn that question around, could you tell me what drew you to this episode? To sum up, if there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: begin with people, not with posters. That experience taught me to ask for help early. Thanks again for having me.

feedback.es: Un buen invitado abre con cortesía, cuenta historias con ejemplos y cifras, devuelve una pregunta de sondeo y cierra con una síntesis.

origin.text: Eres invitado de un pódcast. Escribe unas 130–300 palabras: apertura cortés; una respuesta con historia (situación, hecho anterior con pasado perfecto, acción y resultado con presente perfecto); otra con ejemplo y cifras; una pregunta de sondeo al anfitrión con «If I may turn that around…»; y un cierre con síntesis.

evidenceGroups: it is a pleasure to be
if i may turn the question

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta y elige su valoración.

choices.text: It is strong: it gives an example and figures.
It is strong: it tells a story with a lesson.
It is vague: there is no concrete example or result.

feedback.es: «A lot of things» y «it went well» son frases de relleno: la respuesta carece de ejemplo y de resultado medible.

origin.audio: Honestly, I did a lot of things, and it went well. People were happy, I think.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una pregunta indirecta bien formada para el anfitrión?

choices.text: Could you tell me what made you choose this topic?
Could you tell me what did you choose this topic?
Could you tell me what this topic you chose made?

feedback.es: En la pregunta indirecta el orden es afirmativo: what made you choose, sin did.

prompt.es: Completa: «Desde entonces, el pódcast ha tenido mil oyentes.»

feedback.es: Since then con un efecto que llega hasta hoy exige presente perfecto: has had.

origin.text: Since then, the podcast ___ had a thousand listeners.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor frase de cierre con síntesis.

choices.text: If there is one takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start small.
I do not know what else to say.

feedback.es: Un cierre con síntesis resume una idea clave para los oyentes; las otras no aportan nada.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame responder brevemente con una historia.»

answer.text: Let me answer briefly with a story

feedback.es: Let me answer briefly… anuncia una respuesta corta y estructurada con una historia.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podrías decirme por qué elegiste ese tema?»

feedback.es: Tras why el orden es afirmativo: why you chose, sin did.

origin.text: Could you tell me why you ___ that topic?
